title: Capability
description: An abstract, vendor/model-neutral statement of what an executor can do. A Capability names the kind(s) of capability it satisfies, never a specific model or vendor.

kind.description: An abstract capability class using the same free-form vocabulary as Promise.kind, such as 'text-generation' or 'code-execution'. Must never name a specific model or vendor.

auth_transport.description: How an executor authenticates to perform this capability: 'subscription_cli', 'oauth_cli', 'local', 'metered_api', or 'api_key'. See docs/executors.md for the vocabulary and how policies gate on it.

interactive.description: Whether performing this capability requires a human present during execution (e.g. an interactive CLI prompt), as opposed to running unattended.

context_window.description: The maximum context size, in tokens, the executor supports for this capability.

platform.description: The platform this capability runs on (e.g. 'macos', 'linux'). An open, illustrative string, not a fixed enum -- per docs/ontology.md's convention for peripheral vocabulary like proof_type/resource_type.

availability.description: Capability-advertised static/informational availability metadata (e.g. 'generally-available', 'beta'). An open, illustrative string, not a fixed enum -- per docs/ontology.md's convention for peripheral vocabulary like proof_type/resource_type. Distinct from and not synchronized with Executor.health()'s live ExecutorAvailability signal in src/praxis_executors/interface.py.
